title: Adaptive refinement of the half-wave wire dipole at 10 GHz fed by a lumped port: passes from three elements per wavelength until its reflection changes by less than 0.02
source: Energy conservation (the power the port delivers is the power radiated through the Huygens box, the structure being lossless) and the directivity of a half-wave dipole with a sinusoidal current, D = (4/Cin(2π)) [cos(π/2 cos θ)/sin θ]² (C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed., Wiley 2016, §4.6)

quantities.quantity: radiated power over the power the port delivers, on the adapted mesh
quantities.reason: two independent integrals of one solution, ½ Re(V I*) at the gap and ½ Re ∮ E × H* · dS round the antenna: 0.9974 after two passes (79 554 then 124 328 unknowns), against 0.9948 for the uniform four elements per wavelength (halfwave-dipole, 109 852 unknowns): half the imbalance at about the same unknowns
the closed form assumes a thin wire's sinusoidal current; this one is λ/60 thick with a 1 mm gap: +2.8 % (+2.1 % uniform, +1.1 % after a third pass), the wire's physics rather than the mesh

quantities.quantity: the feed's reflection's change at the last pass
quantities.reason: converged: the loop's own criterion (8.4e-3 at pass 2; the input impedance 110.4 + j27.9 → 110.3 + j25.9 Ω, against 110.9 + j27.9 uniform)
